chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man gives charity to his child as a specific charity gift, he inherits it; but if he gives it as charity to a cause that he dedicates for God's sake, it is not due to him (i.e., he does not inherit it).

key_terms.يَنْبَغِي لَهُ: is due to him / belongs to him

ai.seo_question: Does a father inherit from the gifts he gives to his children?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Baqir to clarify the legal distinction between a father's gift (hibah) to his child, which remains the child's property and is thus inheritable by the father, and a charitable dedication (sadaqah li-wajh Allah), which is for God's sake and not inheritable. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that a father retains inheritance rights from his children unless the gift is explicitly designated as a permanent charity for God's pleasure.
